answer: The cost lands per head: 90 aliases need 90 records, each checked live against the issuer, so bulk forgery costs 90 times what one honest seat costs. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. Entry needs deep sea research cruise participation log: cruises sailed with one institute across years of ocean surveys. The voyage is the bottleneck and the gale is the receipt: a farm must clear both for each of its 90 aliases, the grove trail is public, and one honest agent clears them once.
